proof.criterion: The blocking finding: the margin check's renewal rule must reject the exact boundary, `3H + call_budget == lifetime`, which is the state the interval was moved from 100 s to 90 s to leave behind - and its remedies must prescribe values that pass the rule they are printed by.
proof.surface: The script the required lint job runs, driven against the real tree with the reviewer's own reachable constant, and its own suite.
proof.observed: The comparison is `renewal_window >= lifetime.value`. The failure now names which side of the boundary it rejects - `are <W> ms, equal to / past the session record lifetime of <L> ms, and the sum must fall strictly short of it: equal is refused as surely as past, because either way the third refresh does not complete before the record expires`. Both remedies moved with it, which was the sharper half: `(lifetime - call_budget) // RENEWALS` prescribed the tie itself whenever that subtraction divides by three, and at today's numbers it gave exactly 96583 ms, whose window is 300000 ms. The suggested maximum is now the largest value that passes, rounded down to a whole second because the daemon's two copies of the heartbeat are parsed as whole seconds or minutes; the suggested minimum lifetime is the first whole second past the sum. The check exits 0 at `280250 ms, strictly inside the session record lifetime 300000 ms`; the suite exits 0 with `Results: 99 passed, 0 failed`.
proof.negativeControl: The reviewer's reachability proof, re-run in the real tree rather than taken from its comment: `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` set to `14_875` gives a 30000 ms call budget and a renewal window of exactly 300000 ms, where the check exited 0 before this round and now exits 1 with `equal to the session record lifetime of 300000 ms ... equal is refused as surely as past`, then `::error::1 problem(s)`. Applying the failure's own suggested maximum heartbeat (89000 ms, with the daemon's `Heartbeat` and `pluginHeartbeat` moved with it as the message says) gives exit 0 at 297000 ms; applying its suggested lifetime (301 s, with `listenerSessionTTL`) gives exit 0 at 300000 ms strictly inside 301000 ms - so both remedies now satisfy the rule that printed them. Every constant was put back and jj diff --stat showed only the intended files. The suite's new tie case asserts the advice as well as the exit code, so the arithmetic cannot drift back onto the boundary.

proof.criterion: The seventh fence site the architect ruled in: `settleEndedHolds` restores a failed hand-back only where a newer move has not settled that topic, without reopening the leak round 2 closed.
proof.surface: The plugin's own test suite, driving a move abandoned mid-hand-back with two failed holds, one of whose roles a newer claim has since taken.
proof.observed: 847 pass, 0 fail (846 before), three runs at 41-43 s. The restore loop skips a failed hold whose topic is the role this process now holds, which is the only trace a newer claim leaves on a topic: it deletes that topic from `abandonedHolds` and drops every pending hand-back of it, so a deletion cannot be detected from the entry, while `claimedRoleTopic === topic` can. No hold the loop hands back is of the role it holds while live, so the condition never matches a live pass. The new case asserts both halves at the surface: the hold nothing settled is handed back, and the one the newer claim settled is not reintroduced and provokes no second claim.
proof.negativeControl: Two mutations, each run against the case alone. Disabling the new `continue` fails it with `["legion-controller@ses_ru"]` where it expects no claim - the redundant soft claim of a role the session already holds, which is the tester's own trace. Making the loop restore nothing fails it the other way, with `notifications.role.reviewer@ses_ru` no longer handed back, so the case cannot pass by the loop doing nothing. envoy.ts was restored byte-for-byte after each, verified by sha256.

filesChanged: .github/scripts/check-heartbeat-margin.sh - rule 1's comparison is strict, its failure names which side of the boundary it rejects, both remedies prescribe values that pass it, the header's statement of the rule matches the comparison, the success line reads `strictly inside`, the two-interval rule and its term are deleted with the backstop paragraph kept under rule 1, and the rules below are renumbered.

.github/scripts/check-heartbeat-margin.test.sh - the tie case at `3H + call_budget == lifetime`, reached by moving the call budget as the reviewer reached it, asserting the advice as well as the exit code; two cases applying the two remedies and passing; the `3H == TTL` case relabelled for what it proves; the deleted rule's case and assertions removed.
packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts - one `continue` and its comment in `settleEndedHolds`' restore loop.
trickyParts: The restore loop's condition had to come from what a newer claim actually does to a topic rather than from a general notion of newness: a claim deletes that topic from `abandonedHolds` and drops every pending hand-back of it, so by the time the loop runs there is nothing left in either map to compare against, and `claimedRoleTopic === topic` is the only trace. It cannot match a live pass, because no hold this loop hands back is of the role the pass holds.

The fence stays below the restore loop, not above it. Round 2 moved it there to stop a failed hand-back being dropped from both maps and leaked; this round narrows what is restored instead, so both defects stay closed.

The suggested maximum heartbeat and the suggested minimum lifetime are rounded to whole seconds rather than being exact millisecond bounds, because the daemon's two copies of the heartbeat and the registry's ttl are parsed only as whole seconds or minutes: a millisecond remedy could never satisfy the copy-equality rules it would have to pass next.
deviations: The architect named one more thing than the reviewer did - the `settleEndedHolds` restore - and that is the third item here. `registerSession`'s stamp is deliberately left unfenced, as ruled, and the pull request body now says why rather than leaving it to the handoff: a stale answer stamps the session the registration really was accepted for, so the backstop treats the new session as unregistered and posts one extra registration outside the queues. That is the safe direction; a fence there would let a stale answer suppress a registration the new session needs.

Nothing else was built. One thing the check still carries was found while working and is reported rather than fixed, per the architect's instruction to bring a fourth item before building it: when the call budget alone reaches the lifetime, the suggested maximum heartbeat comes out negative. The formula had that shape before this round too, and it is reachable only from a tree that is already failing for a larger reason.
discoveredComplexity: A remedy printed by a guard is part of the guard: `(lifetime - call_budget) // RENEWALS` was correct for a non-strict rule and prescribed the rejected boundary for a strict one, so making the comparison strict without moving the arithmetic would have left a check whose own advice fails it. The suite now asserts the advice, which is what stops that returning.
